title: Capture Engram's per-request phase trace (ENGRAM_MCP_PHASE_TRACE) for control incidents and show it as an expandable card diagnostic (Greg 2026-10-11)
outcome: Per Greg's direction via Engram::Advisor (TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #589, 2026-10-11 02:34Z): Engram already offers ENGRAM_MCP_PHASE_TRACE=1, bounded JSON-line phase events on stderr correlated by request id, but TermAl's cards don't retain or attach them, so a 20 s control incident can't say whether process creation, begin, the response wait or the acknowledgement stalled. Deliver: (1) a bounded per-request capture plan: phase, elapsed time, classification/code, correlation id, retained only for the incident's request or in a bounded ring (no unbounded logging); (2) a UI diagnostic plan: normal UI stays concise, and the detail is expandable on the control card (coordinated with w-5b823829eb80's expandable section and w-cfcf10b68c9b's C11(c) host phase split); (3) the exact config decision it needs (how the trace is enabled for the host's Engram control processes), named for Greg, NOT enabled globally by this item. A plan first, then implementation after the decision.
acceptance: The coordinator/Advisor receives this capture/UI/config plan with exact producer correlation, bounds, peer contracts and unresolved configuration choice; no code/config is changed before the decision.

After recorded scope/config decision, capture is bounded and independently drained, correlates exact process/frame/request/card across timeout/replacement/late lines, retains only permitted normalized incident data, and diagnostics never decide authority/retry/credit (test-bound at implementation).

Cards retain concise normal/recovered presentation, show optional expandable host/Engram phase diagnostics with honest partial/loss/disabled status, and older cards remain compatible (test-bound at implementation).
Exact-input full gate and independent Codex/Claude pair pass before an implementation landing.
